The speakers argue that the cybersecurity industry has historically placed an unfair burden on end-users through security awareness training rather than demanding secure software development from vendors.

The Secure-by-Design Imperative

CISA’s Secure-by-Design initiative urges software manufacturers to eliminate entire classes of vulnerabilities (such as memory-safety flaws and default credentials) before products ship.

Building Public-Private Accountability

Fostering long-term systemic resilience requires policy frameworks that align market incentives with rigorous software transparency, corporate accountability, and open vulnerability disclosure.

talks.title: Legend of Zelda: Use-After-Free
talks.teaser: Allan Cecil details how a Use-After-Free flaw in Ocarina of Time allowed TASBot to execute arbitrary code on an unmodified Nintendo 64 to raise $228K for charity.
talks.summary:
Hacking the Nintendo 64 via Controller Inputs

Tool-Assisted Speedruns (TAS) push vintage console hardware to its physical limits, leveraging frame-perfect controller inputs to trigger esoteric memory corruption vulnerabilities.

Exploiting a Use-After-Free in Ocarina of Time

Allan Cecil explains how a subtle Use-After-Free vulnerability in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time’s actor management system permits hijacking game execution flow.

Multi-Stage Bootstrapping via TASBot

Using the custom hardware robot TASBot, precise button sequences streamed arbitrary MIPS assembly code into console RAM, bootstrapping a full arbitrary code execution engine on an unmodified retail N64.

Charity Showcase and Cultural Impact

The live exploit demonstration at Summer Games Done Quick (SGDQ) 2022 generated over $228,000 for charity, demonstrating the positive community impact of exploit engineering.

talks.title: J4 Gate: The Hustler Poker Cheating Scandal Investigation
talks.teaser: Scott Melnick recounts his technical investigation into the infamous Hustler Casino Live $240K poker hand, examining live-stream RFID security and cheating hypotheses.
talks.summary:
The Infamous Hustler Casino Live $240K Hand

In September 2022, an unprecedented all-in call for a $240,000 cash pot on the Hustler Casino Live stream ignited accusations of high-tech cheating across the international poker community.

Investigating Live-Stream Table RFID Architecture

Scott Melnick conducts a technical forensic analysis of broadcast poker tables, evaluating the RFID readers, embedded table antennas, production video feeds, and backstage employee access controls.

Evaluating Potential Cheating Vectors and Collusion

The investigation explores potential exploit vectors, including compromised RFID card telemetry, covert vibrating wearables, rogue wireless transmitters, and insider collusion.

Lessons in Community Sleuthing and Integrity

Melnick shares insights from 26 years in the hacker community, illustrating how open-source investigative methods and peer collaboration uncover technical anomalies in live gaming environments.

talks.title: Internet Censorship: What Governments Have in Store for You
talks.teaser: A panel of international technologists and digital rights advocates examine escalating state internet censorship, legal crackdowns, and circumvention tools.
talks.summary:
The Global Erosion of Internet Freedom

Authoritarian regimes and backsliding democracies alike are enacting restrictive telecommunications laws, centralized internet kill switches, and aggressive filtering apparatuses to control citizen information access.

Technological Mechanisms of State Censorship

Panelists analyze the deployment of nationwide Deep Packet Inspection (DPI), DNS poisoning, BGP route manipulation, and targeted throttling against independent media and privacy tools.

Legal and Regulatory Pressures on Encryption

Governments increasingly introduce legislation targeting end-to-end encrypted messaging, open-source privacy software, and VPN providers under the guise of public safety.

Building Resilient Circumvention Ecosystems

The session emphasizes the necessity for global hacker collaboration in developing decentralized, pluggable transport protocols and censorship-resistant communication infrastructure.

talks.title: Unparalleled RDP Monitoring Reveals Attackers' Tradecraft
talks.teaser: Gozint and ESET researchers use PyRDP to record and classify over 100 hours of attacker sessions on exposed RDP honeypots into behavioral archetypes.
talks.summary:
The Primacy of RDP in Ransomware Intrusions

Exposed Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) services represent one of the most frequent initial access vectors exploited by cybercriminals and opportunistic ransomware operators.

Deploying PyRDP for In-Depth Session Interception

Maxime Bergeron and Olivier Bilodeau deploy PyRDP, an open-source man-in-the-middle RDP proxy that records keystrokes, clipboard transfers, mapped drives, and video playback of live intrusions.

Categorizing Attacker Archetypes via D&D Taxonomy

Analyzing over 100 hours of video recordings reveals distinct behavioral archetypes—ranging from noisy brute-force 'Barbarians' to stealthy reconnaissance 'Rangers' and proxying 'Wizards'.

Translating Honeypot Telemetry into Blue-Team Defenses

Documenting common command sequences, tooling artifacts, and monetization strategies enables defensive teams to build robust detection rules against real-world lateral movement.

talks.title: How an Auto Security Researcher Had His Car Stolen
talks.teaser: Automotive security experts reverse engineer a real-world CAN Injection theft tool disguised as a Bluetooth speaker used to steal a Toyota RAV4.
talks.summary:
Investigating the Theft of a 2021 Toyota RAV4

When automotive security researcher Ian Tabor's vehicle was stolen from his driveway, he tracked down physical forensic evidence pointing to an emerging attack method known as CAN Injection.

Reverse Engineering the Hardware Theft Tool

Ian Tabor and Ken Tindell acquire and dissect the criminal hardware device—cleverly concealed inside a modified JBL Bluetooth speaker enclosure.

Exploiting Headlight Wiring to Inject CAN Frames

By accessing the vehicle's CAN bus wiring behind the front bumper headlight assembly, the rogue device silences legitimate Electronic Control Units (ECUs) and injects forged door-unlock and immobilizer-disable commands.

Industry Remediation and Cryptographic Message Authentication

The authors detail their coordinated vulnerability disclosure with Toyota, urging automakers to adopt cryptographic CAN message authentication (SecOC) to thwart physical bus injection.

talks.title: HL7Magic: Medical Data Hacking Made Easy
talks.teaser: Katie Inns introduces HL7Magic, an open-source Burp Suite extension enabling security researchers to intercept, decode, and tamper with legacy HL7 medical device traffic.
talks.summary:
The Insecurity of Legacy Healthcare Protocols

While modern healthcare APIs adopt HTTP-based FHIR standards, critical hospital systems and embedded diagnostic devices still rely universally on legacy Health Level Seven (HL7) protocol formats.

The Lack of Tooling for Proprietary Medical Protocols

HL7 messages utilize bespoke non-HTTP framing that cannot be natively inspected, parsed, or modified by standard commercial penetration testing suites.

Introducing the HL7Magic Burp Suite Extension

Katie Inns presents HL7Magic, an open-source extension that intercepts raw TCP HL7 socket streams, decodes segment delimiters, and integrates seamlessly into Burp Suite's Repeater and Intruder.

Demonstrating Medical Device Vulnerabilities

Live demonstrations illustrate how tampering with HL7 patient identifiers and telemetry payloads can misattribute medical records, highlighting patient safety risks in clinical environments.

talks.title: Hacker Court Interactive Scenario
talks.teaser: An interactive courtroom simulation where DEF CON attendees act as jurors in a cybercrime trial, learning legal attribution standards and forensic evidence handling.
talks.summary:
Simulating a High-Stakes Cybercrime Prosecution

Hacker Court brings trial attorneys, forensic expert witnesses, and security researchers together in an interactive mock trial prosecuting a complex intrusion scenario.

The Challenges of Digital Attribution

Prosecutors and defense counsel spar over digital forensic artifacts, debating whether IP logs, shellcode signatures, and server telemetry constitute definitive proof or a deceptive false flag.

Crucial Evidence Handling for Incident Responders

The trial highlights the strict legal thresholds required for evidence admissibility, teaching detection and response engineers what forensic data must be preserved during an active breach.

Jury Deliberation and Verdict

The audience serves as the trial jury, evaluating circumstantial versus technical evidence to render a live verdict on the hacker's guilt or innocence.

talks.title: WINE Pairing with Malware
talks.teaser: Jared Stroud configures WINE and Valve Proton gaming compatibility layers on Linux as lightweight, local malware analysis sandboxes to extract IoCs.
talks.summary:
Repurposing Gaming Compatibility Layers for Malware Analysis

The rapid evolution of WINE and Proton for running modern Windows video games on Linux provides a robust runtime environment capable of executing Windows PE malware.

Configuring Lightweight Linux Triage Environments

Jared Stroud demonstrates setting up headless WINE environments on Linux to execute unknown malware samples without expensive commercial sandbox infrastructure.

Extracting IoCs Using Native UNIX Utilities

Leveraging standard command-line tools like awk, grep, strace, and network packet capture utilities enables rapid extraction of forensic indicators and C2 network endpoints.

Accelerating Offense-Defense Iteration Cycles

The presentation illustrates how malware authors and defensive analysts can use WINE environments to rapidly test implants, validate evasion techniques, and shorten feedback loops.

talks.title: XR Village Fireside Chat
talks.teaser: Human rights attorney Brittan Heller discusses biometric privacy, spatial computing ethics, and civil liberties in immersive environments.

talks.title: What 10 Years of Drive Stats Data Can Tell Us
talks.teaser: Andy Klein presents a decade of longitudinal Backblaze Drive Stats data, analyzing failure metrics, lifetime telemetry, and reliability trends across enterprise storage drives.

talks.title: The History of XR: From Fiction to Reality
talks.teaser: Traces the evolution of extended reality from sci-fi concepts into practical spatial computing hardware and platforms.

talks.title: The Importance of Arts and Crafts in ThreatOps
talks.teaser: Pete Hay presents visual diagramming frameworks to communicate complex threat intelligence, incident timelines, and multi-stage attack graphs in ThreatOps.
talks.summary:
The Visual Communication Challenge in Incident Response

Cybersecurity analysts frequently struggle to convey complex multi-stage intrusions to non-technical executive stakeholders and cross-functional engineering teams.

Overcoming Divergent Threat Modeling Diagrams

Pete Hay identifies that asking multiple analysts to map the same incident yields conflicting, disorganized diagrams that obscure critical attack paths.

Standardizing ThreatOps Visual Frameworks

The presentation introduces structured visual templates for diagramming adversary campaigns, Kill Chain stages, lateral movement pivots, and infrastructure clusters.

Enhancing Incident Reporting and Decision-Making

High-density, visually intuitive diagrams accelerate executive incident decision-making and improve operational coordination across detection and response teams.

talks.title: Hack the Future: Why Congress & White House Support AI Red Teaming
talks.teaser: White House and Congressional leaders discuss government backing for the DEF CON Generative AI Red Team exercise to evaluate commercial LLM risks.
talks.summary:
Government Collaboration with the Hacker Community

The White House, National Science Foundation, and Congressional AI Caucus formally partnered with DEF CON's AI Village to host the largest public Generative AI Red Team exercise.

Balancing Rapid AI Innovation with Emerging Risks

Austin Carson and federal leaders discuss the policy challenges of managing generative AI deployment across critical infrastructure, national security, and civil society.

Democratizing Public Trust and Safety Evaluations

Enabling thousands of independent hackers to stress-test frontier models from major AI providers creates transparent benchmarks for model hallucinations, bias, and vulnerability surfaces.

Institutionalizing Independent Red Teaming in AI Policy

The panel explores how lessons from public red-teaming exercises will inform future federal AI procurement standards and executive governance frameworks.

talks.title: Growing the Community of AI Hackers with the Generative Red Team
talks.teaser: AI Village organizers share the architecture and methodology behind the largest public Generative AI Red Team challenge testing frontier models at DEF CON 31.
talks.summary:
Organizing the Largest Public AI Red Teaming Event

The AI Village at DEF CON 31 assembled frontier models from Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI, Stability AI, and others on an evaluation platform built by Scale AI.

Shifting Beyond Prompt Injections and Jailbreaks

Sven Cattell, Rumman Chowdhury, and Austin Carson explain that evaluating Large Language Models requires testing stochastic behaviors, demographic biases, and hallucination propagation.

The Evolution of Algorithmic and Bias Bounties

The organizers trace the history of algorithmic bounty programs, detailing how probabilistic software flaws require reimagined bug reporting, verification, and payout structures.

Building an Inclusive Global AI Security Community

Providing accessible red-teaming platforms empowers multidisciplinary researchers to develop standardized methodologies for auditing foundation AI models.

talks.title: GhostToken: Exploiting GCP to Create Unremovable Trojan Apps
talks.teaser: Tal Skverer details GhostToken, a critical zero-day vulnerability in Google Cloud Platform allowing third-party OAuth apps to become invisible and unremovable.
talks.summary:
OAuth 2.0 Integrations in Enterprise Cloud Platforms

Modern SaaS ecosystems rely heavily on third-party OAuth applications, where users grant scoped API tokens allowing external services to access email, documents, and cloud storage.

The Architectural Coupling of Google Accounts and GCP

Tal Skverer analyzes Google's migration requiring all third-party marketplace applications to be tethered to underlying Google Cloud Platform (GCP) developer projects.

Discovering the GhostToken Zero-Day Vulnerability

Manipulating GCP project deletion states places third-party OAuth applications into an unlisted 'pending deletion' limbo where valid access tokens persist indefinitely while disappearing from user management dashboards.

Creating Permanent, Invisible Backdoor Access

Exploiting GhostToken enabled an attacker to maintain persistent, unremovable access to a victim's Google Workspace data without any visible indicator in account security settings.

talks.title: Getting a Migraine: Unique SIP Bypass on macOS
talks.teaser: Discloses 'Migraine', a novel macOS System Integrity Protection (SIP) bypass vulnerability allowing root users to load unsigned kernel extensions.
talks.summary:
The Security Boundary of macOS System Integrity Protection

System Integrity Protection (SIP) restricts root-level capabilities in macOS, preventing the modification of core system binaries, filesystem trees, and the loading of unsigned kernel extensions.

Reverse Engineering Apple Migration Assistant

Nir Even Or, Phil Pearse, and Ankur Bohra audit macOS system maintenance daemons, discovering critical logic oversights in how Apple's Migration Assistant executes elevated maintenance routines.

Bypassing SIP to Install Undeletable Malware

Exploiting the 'Migraine' vulnerability allows an attacker with root privileges to completely bypass SIP enforcement, modify protected directories, and load arbitrary kernel extensions.

Detection Strategies and Vendor Remediation

The researchers present behavioral detection heuristics for endpoint monitoring and review Apple's coordinated security patch.

talks.title: Game Changing Advances in Windows Shellcode Analysis
talks.teaser: Dr. Bramwell Brizendine introduces SHAREM, an advanced shellcode emulation framework providing complete code coverage and flawless Ghidra disassembly.
talks.summary:
The Difficulties of Analyzing Obfuscated Shellcode

Malicious shellcode frequently employs custom encoding, environment hashing, and dynamic API resolving, causing static disassemblers like IDA Pro and Ghidra to produce incomplete or corrupted output.

Introducing the SHAREM Emulation Engine

Dr. Bramwell Brizendine, Austin Kersten, and Max Hince present SHAREM, a specialized emulation framework capable of emulating over 20,000 Windows API functions and 99% of system calls.

Achieving Complete Code Coverage via Snapshot Restores

SHAREM records CPU register contexts and memory state at every control flow fork; when execution terminates, it restores previous states to explore all divergent code branches.

Flawless Disassembly and Ghidra Plugin Integration

Integrating SHAREM’s runtime emulation data with a custom Ghidra plugin automatically resolves decoded shellcode, reconstructs obfuscated strings, and labels identified API calls.

talks.title: From Feature to Weapon: Breaking Microsoft Teams and SharePoint
talks.teaser: Dr. Nestori Syynimaa abuses SharePoint Online migration APIs to tamper with files, inject stored XSS, and escalate privileges across Microsoft Teams and Azure AD.
talks.summary:
SharePoint Online as Universal Enterprise Storage

Microsoft SharePoint Online (SPO) serves as the foundational file repository for Microsoft 365, powering backend document management for Teams channels, OneDrive, and Office Groups.

Abusing Granular Migration APIs

Dr. Nestori Syynimaa audits Microsoft migration utilities (Migration Manager and SPMT), discovering that their underlying REST APIs lack strict tenant-level integrity verification.

Tampering with Shared Files and Injecting Stored XSS

An unprivileged tenant user can leverage migration endpoints to overwrite existing documents, forge file creation timestamps, and inject malicious scripts into SharePoint lists.

Cross-Service Privilege Escalation to Azure AD

Triggering stored XSS within Microsoft Teams and SharePoint execution contexts enables stealing administrative access tokens, leading to full tenant elevation of privilege in Azure Active Directory.

talks.title: Fireside Chat with the National Cyber Director
talks.teaser: Acting National Cyber Director Kemba Walden discusses the implementation of the National Cybersecurity Strategy, workforce development, and public-private defense.

talks.title: Fantastic Ethertypes and Where to Find Them
talks.teaser: Ricky Lawshae explores esoteric non-IP Ethernet protocols across transportation, industrial SCADA, and healthcare networks, demonstrating packet injection vectors.
talks.summary:
Exploring Beyond the TCP/IP Protocol Stack

While most security monitoring focuses exclusively on IP-based traffic, Layer 2 Ethernet frames support hundreds of specialized, non-routable protocols defined by distinct EtherType fields.

Surveying Esoteric Ethertypes in the Wild

Ricky Lawshae investigates obscure Ethernet protocols deployed in industrial manufacturing plants, rail transportation networks, and hospital clinical facilities.

Security Implications of Unauthenticated Layer 2 Protocols

Many specialized EtherType implementations lack basic authentication, encryption, or sequence validation, allowing local network attackers to inject control commands directly.

Defensive Visibility and Network Segmentation

The presentation demonstrates packet crafting tools for auditing non-IP protocols and provides network architecture recommendations for Layer 2 filtering.

talks.title: Exploring Linux Memory Manipulation for Stealth and Evasion
talks.teaser: Carlos Polop and Javier Gutierrez demonstrate novel in-memory manipulation techniques on Linux to execute stealthy payloads within read-only and distroless containers.
talks.summary:
Exploitation Challenges in Hardened Linux Environments

Modern container deployments increasingly utilize read-only root filesystems, `noexec` volume mounts, and minimal distroless base images to restrict attacker payload execution.

Manipulating Linux Memory Without Executable Disk Files

Carlos Polop and Javier Gutierrez explore advanced in-memory execution primitives, abusing `ptrace`, `/proc/self/mem`, and fileless shared memory file descriptors (`memfd_create`).

Process Injection and Runtime Code Patching

Step-by-step demonstrations illustrate how malicious implants can inject shellcode into running daemon memory spaces, hook dynamic symbols, and evade container security monitors.

Mitigations and Container Hardening

The authors discuss defensive countermeasures, including restricting `ptrace_scope`, deploying Seccomp system call filters, and implementing kernel-level memory integrity auditing.

talks.title: Exploiting OPC UA: Practical Attacks Against OPC UA Architectures
talks.teaser: Claroty Team82 reveals critical vulnerabilities across OPC UA protocol stack implementations, demonstrating remote code execution across industrial SCADA networks.
talks.summary:
OPC UA as the Backbone of Industrial Automation

Open Platform Communications Unified Architecture (OPC UA) is the industry standard protocol connecting physical OT sensors, SCADA servers, and corporate IT management networks.

Auditing OPC UA Protocol Stack Implementations

Noam Moshe and Sharon Brizinov conduct an extensive two-year evaluation of major commercial and open-source OPC UA stacks powering millions of industrial devices.

Uncovering Critical Protocol Specification Pitfalls

Fuzzing complex protocol features—including method invocations, message chunking, certificate validation, and complex data variants—revealed multiple RCE and DoS zero-days.

Releasing Open-Source Exploitation Tooling

The researchers release an open-source auditing framework, providing OT asset owners and equipment vendors with tools to verify and patch OPC UA deployments.

talks.title: ELECTRONizing macOS Privacy: A New Weapon in Your Red Teaming Armory
talks.teaser: Wojciech Reguła demonstrates hijacking Electron application configurations on macOS to inherit high-privilege TCC permissions without zero-days.
talks.summary:
The Privacy Architecture of macOS TCC

Apple's Transparency, Consent, and Control (TCC) subsystem enforces strict sandboxing on macOS, requiring explicit user authorization to access files, webcams, microphones, and screens.

The Inherent Vulnerabilities of Ubiquitous Electron Apps

Wojciech Reguła identifies that widely used Electron desktop applications (such as Slack, Teams, and Discord) hold extensive TCC entitlements granted by users.

Abusing Default Electron Configurations to Inherit Permissions

Manipulating insecure runtime flags, dynamic node integration parameters, and environment variables allows executing arbitrary code inside existing Electron processes to inherit their TCC rights.

Releasing Open-Source Tooling for Red and Blue Teams

Reguła releases an open-source exploitation tool for red teams while providing SOC defenders with endpoint detection telemetry rules to flag Electron process tampering.

talks.title: Push All the Buttons: Digital Twinning with Idaho National Laboratory
talks.teaser: Details how Idaho National Laboratory uses XR digital twins to model, simulate, and stress-test critical infrastructure control systems.

talks.title: Designing RFID Implants: Flipping the Bird Opens Doors
talks.teaser: Miana Ella Windall chronicles designing and implanting custom subdermal RFID credentials to interact seamlessly with proprietary workplace access control readers.
talks.summary:
The Landscape of Subdermal RFID Implants

Subdermal RFID and NFC microchips allow individuals to store cryptographic credentials, transit passes, and medical identifiers directly beneath the skin.

Overcoming Compatibility Limits in Commercial Implants

When commercial transponders failed to support her employer's proprietary building access control readers, Miana Ella Windall engineered a bespoke implant transponder.

Antenna Design and Biocompatible Packaging

Designing custom subdermal hardware required tuning micro-coil antenna inductance for 13.56 MHz/125 kHz resonance and encapsulating the silicon inside medical-grade biopolymers.

Future Implications for Physical Authentication

Windall shares lessons in amateur hardware prototyping, biological safety protocols, and the ethical future of implanted personal authentication credentials.

talks.title: Defending KA-SAT
talks.teaser: Viasat engineers share the inside story of responding to the 2022 AcidRain wiper attack against the KA-SAT satellite network during the invasion of Ukraine.
talks.summary:
The Historic Cyberattack on the KA-SAT Satellite Network

In February 2022, coinciding with the Russian military invasion of Ukraine, an adversary launched a devastating destructive cyberattack against Viasat's European KA-SAT network.

Rapid Forensic Analysis of Impacted Satellite Terminals

Mark Colaluca and Nick Saunders describe how Viasat engineers conducted emergency hardware forensics, discovering within 36 hours that terminal flash memory had been overwritten by a wiper.

Reverse Engineering the AcidRain Wiper

Reverse engineering the malicious toolkit revealed a targeted wiper designed to overwrite MTD storage partitions and brick tens of thousands of satellite ground modems.

Mitigating Ongoing Electronic and Network Assaults

The authors detail how operational teams defended against sustained over-the-air network attacks for weeks following the initial incident to restore critical European communications.

talks.title: Defender Pretender: When Windows Defender Updates Become a Security Risk
talks.teaser: Discloses a zero-day vulnerability in Windows Defender signature updates, allowing unprivileged users to neutralize EDR protections and run malware fully undetected.
talks.summary:
The Critical Role of Antivirus Signature Updates

Endpoint security engines rely on continuous signature definition updates to identify emerging threats, requiring robust cryptographic validation of downloaded signature files.

Reverse Engineering Windows Defender Update Mechanisms

Omer Attias and Amit Bar dissect the internal architecture of Windows Defender, analyzing the proprietary signature database format and local update validation pipelines.

Unprivileged EDR Neutralization via Defender-Pretender

Discovering a critical logic flaw allows unprivileged users to inject manipulated signature definitions, completely neutralizing threat detection and allowing known malware to execute undetected.

Coercing Defender into Destructive File Deletion

The researchers demonstrate weaponizing Defender's remediation engine to force the deletion of critical operating system files, resulting in an unrecoverable system crash.

talks.title: Defeating VPN Always On
talks.teaser: Maxime Clementz evaluates Windows VPN Always-On enterprise security controls, demonstrating design and implementation bypasses to reach untrusted networks.
talks.summary:
The Purpose of VPN Always-On Enterprise Controls

Organizations enforce 'VPN Always-On' policies on mobile corporate laptops to ensure all network traffic is encrypted and routed exclusively through corporate security gateways.

Auditing Windows Network APIs and Commercial VPN Clients

Maxime Clementz examines how the Windows networking stack and popular commercial enterprise VPN solutions enforce persistent gateway routing rules.

Discovering Design and Implementation Bypasses

Analyzing DNS resolution flows, local subnet routing exceptions, and captive portal helper daemons reveals methods to bypass network tunneling and reach local networks directly.

Hardening Always-On VPN Deployments

Clementz provides actionable hardening configurations for enterprise network administrators to close routing leakage paths and secure endpoints on untrusted public Wi-Fi.

talks.title: Closing Ceremonies & Awards
talks.teaser: The Dark Tangent and DEF CON senior staff close out DEF CON 31 with official event recaps, community statistics, and Black Badge awards.

talks.title: Death by 1000 Likes: The Online Wall of Sheep
talks.teaser: Will Kay details building an automated OSINT scraper for Reddit to monitor year-round credential leaks, creating a virtual Wall of Sheep.
talks.summary:
Extending the Wall of Sheep Beyond DEF CON

Inspired by DEF CON's famous Packet Hacking Village Wall of Sheep, which displays credentials broadcast over unencrypted convention Wi-Fi, Australian researchers expanded the concept online.

Scraping Social Media for Accidental Information Leaks

Will Kay details developing automated scraping pipelines targeting the r/defcon subreddit and hacker forums between DEF CON 30 and 31.

Analyzing Year-Round Credential and Data Exposure

Aggregating publicly shared photos, badge photos, QR codes, and forum posts reveals persistent operational security lapses among conference attendees year-round.

Lessons in Personal OPSEC and Social Media Hygiene

The presentation highlights how innocuous social media posts can be aggregated into detailed personal profiles, urging attendees to practice disciplined digital hygiene.

talks.title: DC101: Welcome to DEF CON
talks.teaser: Long-time organizers and community members welcome newcomers to DEF CON, sharing tips, cultural norms, and strategies to navigate the world's largest hacker convention.

talks.title: The Risks of Pointing Out the Emperor is Buck Naked
talks.teaser: Renderman and Tom Dang share first-hand accounts of facing legal retaliation when reporting government vulnerabilities, urging reform in public disclosure policies.
talks.summary:
The Chilling Effect of Flawed Disclosure Paths

Despite national public slogans encouraging citizens to report safety concerns, security researchers reporting critical government software vulnerabilities frequently face threats of arrest.

Personal Accounts of Bureaucratic and Legal Retaliation

Renderman and Tom Dang recount personal experiences attempting to report critical flaws in public sector systems, facing aggressive legal investigations, jurisdictional conflicts, and reputational damage.

Root Causes of Disclosure Failures

The speakers analyze the systemic factors that derail coordinated disclosure: ambiguous reporting channels, superseding statutes (like the CFAA), organizational fear, and executive ego.

Building Standardized Safe Harbor Policies

The presentation outlines legislative proposals and practical templates for government agencies to implement binding vulnerability disclosure policies and legal safe harbors.

talks.title: Cracking Cicada 3301
talks.teaser: Leaders of the CicadaSolvers community detail the 9-year collaborative effort to decrypt Cicada 3301's Liber Primus runic cryptogram.
talks.summary:
The Legend of the Cicada 3301 Mystery

First appearing on the internet in 2012, Cicada 3301 released intricate cryptographic challenges combining steganography, classical literature, music theory, and ancient runes.

The Enigma of Liber Primus

Taiiwo, Artorias, Puck, and TheClockworkBird delve into Liber Primus, an encrypted 73-page book written in Elder Futhark runes that has baffled cryptographers since 2014.

Collaborative Cryptanalysis Across Nine Years

The speakers outline the mathematical, linguistic, and statistical cryptanalysis frameworks built by the global CicadaSolvers community to crack the manuscript's remaining pages.

Lessons in Community Resilience and Open Research

The presentation explores how decentralized volunteer communities maintain motivation over nearly a decade of tackling one of the most famous unsolved internet puzzles.

talks.title: Contest Closing Ceremonies & Awards
talks.teaser: The Contest Goons announce competition winners, present awards, and recap tournament highlights across all official contests at DEF CON 31.

talks.title: Staying Undetected Using the Windows Container Isolation Framework
talks.teaser: Daniel Avinoam reverse engineers the Windows Containers minifilter driver, weaponizing native filesystem isolation to hide malicious files and evade EDR sensors.
talks.summary:
The Native Architecture of Windows Containers

Introduced in Windows Server 2016, Windows Containers provide lightweight process-level and Hyper-V filesystem isolation using a built-in kernel minifilter driver.

Reverse Engineering the Container Minifilter Driver

Daniel Avinoam reverse engineers Microsoft's container storage driver, detailing how copy-on-write redirection transparently separates container file modifications from the host volume.

Weaponizing Container Isolation for EDR Evasion

Instead of attempting container escapes, an attacker can intentionally run implants inside a custom container context, blinding host-based EDR agents from observing file drop and execution events.

Releasing Open-Source Tooling and Defensive Strategies

Avinoam releases an open-source proof-of-concept tool demonstrating native container abuse and outlines telemetry signatures for security engineers to detect containerized evasion.

talks.title: Contactless Overflow: Code Execution in Payment Terminals & ATMs
talks.teaser: Josep Rodriguez demonstrates contactless buffer overflow vulnerabilities in NFC payment readers across major ATM and POS brands, enabling ATM jackpotting.
talks.summary:
The Attack Surface of Contactless NFC Payment Readers

NFC payment terminals deployed across major retail stores, gas pumps, and ATMs must parse complex Application Protocol Data Units (APDUs) from unauthenticated wireless taps.

Discovering APDU Buffer Overflows Across Major Vendors

Josep Rodriguez analyzes firmware across seven leading terminal vendors (including IDTech, Ingenico, Verifone, and BBPOS), uncovering memory corruption bugs in APDU parsers.

Compromising Terminals via Malicious Android Taps

Using a custom Android application, an attacker can transmit malformed APDUs during an NFC exchange, executing arbitrary shellcode on bare-metal and embedded Linux readers.

Chaining Host USB Exploits and ATM Jackpotting

Rodriguez demonstrates pivoting from compromised NFC readers over internal USB connections to exploit host operating system SDKs, enabling physical ATM cash dispensing jackpotting.

talks.title: CON-trolling the Weather: Hacking Radiosondes
talks.teaser: Paz Hameiri develops a simulation framework to spoof and jam weather balloon radiosonde telemetry, threatening global climate models and rocket launches.
talks.summary:
The Critical Role of High-Altitude Weather Balloons

Meteorological agencies worldwide launch approximately 1,800 weather balloons daily, transmitting upper-atmosphere atmospheric telemetry used in global climate models and space launches.

Reverse Engineering Radiosonde Payloads

Paz Hameiri analyzes the RF protocols used by dominant radiosonde manufacturers, dissecting telemetry packets measuring pressure, humidity, temperature, and GPS coordinates.

Developing Spoofing and Jamming Simulation Tools

Using software-defined radio (SDR), Hameiri builds a simulation toolkit to forge radiosonde sensor broadcasts and execute targeted jamming against receiver ground stations.

Exposing Vulnerabilities in Military Radiosondes

The author discusses design weaknesses in military-grade radiosonde variants and proposes lightweight cryptographic authentication to prevent data tampering.

talks.title: Civil Cyber Defense
talks.teaser: Tiffany Rad and Austin Shamlin highlight pro-bono civil cyber defense, using OSINT and student clinics to protect human rights organizations and combat human trafficking.
talks.summary:
Protecting Vulnerable Civil Society Organizations

Non-profit organizations, investigative journalists, and human rights defenders face targeted surveillance and harassment from well-resourced adversaries despite possessing minimal IT security budgets.

The UC Berkeley Citizen Clinic Model

Tiffany Rad presents case studies from academic public-interest clinics, demonstrating how student security researchers provide threat modeling, digital hygiene, and defensive hardening to high-risk groups.

Leveraging OSINT to Disrupt Human Trafficking

Austin Shamlin outlines open-source intelligence methodologies used to assist law enforcement in tracking human trafficking rings and identifying illicit operational infrastructure.

Scaling Volunteer and Community Defense

The speakers urge the hacker community to contribute technical expertise and open-source tooling to protect vulnerable non-profit organizations operating on the front lines.

talks.title: Using SIM Tunneling to Travel at Light Speed
talks.teaser: Introduces MobileAtlas, an open-source testbed that decouples physical SIM cards from cellular modems globally to uncover international roaming and metering flaws.
talks.summary:
Challenges in Global Cellular Roaming Research

Auditing international cellular networks requires physical access to diverse carrier roaming partnerships, mobile rate plans, and geographically dispersed base stations.

Introducing the MobileAtlas SIM-Tunneling Framework

Adrian Dabrowski and Gabriel Gegenhuber present MobileAtlas, an open-source measurement platform that decouples physical SIM cards from modems via low-latency network tunnels.

Uncovering Data Metering Flaws and Free-Riding

Auditing commercial carrier roaming configurations revealed widespread traffic accounting discrepancies, enabling zero-rated data consumption and unmetered data tunneling.

Tracking Roaming Victims via Progress Tones

The authors expose widespread IPv6 firewall misconfigurations and demonstrate fingerprinting unique carrier progress audio tones to track victims across international borders.

talks.title: Calling it a 0-Day: Hacking at PBX & UC Systems
talks.teaser: Dissects enterprise Private Branch Exchange (PBX) and Unified Communications platforms, chaining Java execution and PHP decryption bugs to gain root shells.
talks.summary:
The Attack Surface of Enterprise Unified Communications

On-premises Private Branch Exchange (PBX) and Unified Communications (UC) systems manage voice, video conferencing, and messaging across enterprise corporate networks.

Auditing Leading Commercial PBX Platforms

The author audits two widespread enterprise PBX products, analyzing proprietary management web consoles, telephony services, and licensing mechanisms.

Chaining Vulnerabilities from Phone Emulation to RCE

Exploitation steps include spoofing VoIP phone endpoints, decrypting obfuscated proprietary PHP source files, bypassing license checks, and abusing Java `Runtime.exec()` invocations.

Hardening Enterprise Communications Infrastructure

The presentation outlines detection signatures for malicious SIP registration traffic and provides remediation guidance for securing on-premise telephony gateways.

talks.title: Contextualizing The Vulkan Leaks & State-Sponsored Offensive Ops
talks.teaser: Joe Slowik analyzes leaked Russian NTC Vulkan documentation, contextualizing state-sponsored offensive cyber programs, automated scanning, and attack infrastructure.
talks.summary:
Deconstructing the NTC Vulkan Documentation Leaks

In early 2023, leaked internal files from Russian defense contractor NTC Vulkan exposed architectural blueprints for state-sponsored cyber offensive programs including 'Scan-V' and 'Amezit'.

Automating Attack Surface Mapping and Exploitation

Joe Slowik evaluates Scan-V's automated scanning capabilities, which continuously correlate global internet infrastructure vulnerabilities to feed targeted offensive targeting pipelines.

Historical Precedents in State Signals Intelligence

Comparing Vulkan capabilities with historic disclosures—including Russia's SORM, China's Great Cannon, and US intelligence tools—reveals a decade-long trajectory toward industrial-scale cyber operations.

The Proliferation and Industrialization of Offensive Tooling

Slowik warns that state-backed cyber programs have shifted from bespoke intrusion toolkits to standardized, modular enterprise software platforms designed for persistent warfare.

talks.title: Breaking BMC: The Forgotten Key to the Kingdom
talks.teaser: NVIDIA offensive researchers detail chaining a dozen vulnerabilities in AMI MegaRAC BMCs, demonstrating remote exploitation to flash persistent implants into server SPI flash.
talks.summary:
The Baseboard Management Controller as a Critical Threat Vector

Baseboard Management Controllers (BMCs) are autonomous service processors on enterprise server motherboards that manage power states, console redirection, and remote firmware flashing.

Auditing AMI MegaRAC BMC Implementations

Alex Tereshkin and Adam Zabrocki examine the widely deployed AMI MegaRAC BMC codebase on enterprise hardware, mapping out network-accessible IPMI and HTTP management interfaces.

Chaining a Dozen Vulnerabilities to Server Firmware Control

The researchers detail an extensive exploit chain starting from zero-knowledge remote access to memory corruption, privilege escalation, and hypervisor-independent code execution.

Flashing Persistent Malicious Firmware into SPI Flash

Demonstrating permanent firmware flashing into the host server SPI flash illustrates how BMC compromise grants attackers undetectable, OS-reinstall-resilient server control.

talks.title: Badge of Shame: Breaking into Secure Facilities with OSDP
talks.teaser: Dan Petro and David Vargas disclose over a dozen cryptographic and implementation flaws in the Open Supervised Device Protocol (OSDP) securing physical access control.
talks.summary:
The Migration from Wiegand to Encrypted OSDP

Physical access control systems are rapidly replacing unencrypted legacy Wiegand wiring with the Open Supervised Device Protocol (OSDP) to encrypt communications between badge readers and controllers.

Cryptographic Pitfalls and Implementation Blunders in OSDP

Dan Petro and David Vargas uncover systemic design oversights, including flawed AES key exchange routines, plaintext fallback modes, and predictable keystreams.

Constructing In-Line Hardware MITM Interceptors

The authors present a low-cost physical pentesting tool that can be spliced behind wall-mounted RFID badge readers to passively sniff master keys and inject door-unlock commands.

Hardening Physical Access Control Networks

Remediating OSDP deployments requires disabling insecure installation modes, enforcing strict cryptographic pairing profiles, and monitoring serial bus impedance.

talks.title: Backdoor in the Core: Altering Intel x86 Instruction Set at Runtime
talks.teaser: Reverse engineers Intel CPU microcode on Goldmont cores, achieving persistent userspace microcode patching on Linux to create hardware backdoors in x86 execution.
talks.summary:
The Hidden World of CPU Microcode

Modern x86 processors translate complex assembly instructions into sequences of low-level internal micro-operations managed by proprietary, encrypted CPU microcode ROMs.

Reverse Engineering Intel Goldmont Microcode ROM

Mathias Krog and Christian Skovsende analyze Intel Atom CPU microcode, detailing custom tracing tools developed to deconstruct instruction decoding and persistence checks.

Achieving Persistent Microcode Patching from Userspace

Bypassing hardware integrity checks allows applying custom microcode patches directly from unprivileged Linux userspace without requiring vendor cryptographic signatures.

Weaponizing Microcode for Undetectable Hardware Backdoors

The authors demonstrate modifying instruction execution semantics at the hardware core level, creating an operating-system-independent backdoor that subverts kernel access controls.

talks.title: Azure B2C 0-Day: An Exploit Chain from Public Keys to Microsoft Bug Bounty
talks.teaser: John Novak details an exploit chain in Microsoft Azure AD B2C, recovering signing keys to forge administrative tokens across customer tenants and the MSRC portal.
talks.summary:
Azure Active Directory B2C Architecture

Microsoft Azure AD B2C provides customer-facing identity and access management for thousands of global enterprises, government agencies, and the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC).

Discovering Cryptographic Misuse in Token Generation

John Novak investigates the cryptographic token issuance flows in Azure B2C, identifying flawed key derivation routines that leak critical cryptographic material.

Recovering Private Keys and Forging Arbitrary Claims

Novel algebraic cryptanalysis enables recovering the internal token-signing keys, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to mint valid administrative JWTs for any tenant.

Full Tenant Compromise and MSRC Impact

Demonstrating the full exploit chain against the live MSRC bug bounty portal illustrates how an attacker could have accessed unpatched Microsoft vulnerability reports.

talks.title: Automotive USB Fuzzing
talks.teaser: Presents an in-vehicle USB kernel fuzzing framework directly connected to production vehicles, discovering zero-days across Volkswagen, Renault, GM, and AGL.
talks.summary:
The Limitations of Conventional Automotive Media Fuzzing

Automotive security evaluations typically test In-Vehicle Infotainment (IVI) media decoders in isolated desktop emulators rather than testing live hardware connected to in-vehicle buses.

Developing Direct In-Vehicle USB Fuzzing Frameworks

Euntae Jang, Donghyon Jeong, and Jonghyuk Song introduce an automated USB fuzzing harness that connects directly to production vehicle head units over physical USB interfaces.

Fuzzing Automotive Kernel Drivers and Media Parsers

Injecting malformed USB descriptor packets and corrupt media streams uncovered severe memory corruption flaws in operating system kernels and Automotive Grade Linux (AGL) distributions.

Real-World Zero-Days Across Major Automakers

Case studies detail reproducible crash and code execution vulnerabilities identified in production Volkswagen Jetta, Renault Zoe, and Chevrolet Equinox infotainment systems.

talks.title: Augmented Reality and Implications on Mobile Security
talks.teaser: Examines the security and privacy implications of augmented reality sensor frameworks and camera feeds on mobile operating systems.

talks.title: Assessing Security of Certificates at Scale
talks.teaser: Cisco researchers run Batch GCD factorization across 100M+ public X.509 certificates, recovering private RSA keys from low-entropy embedded devices.
talks.summary:
Entropy Failures in Global Key Generation

Flawed pseudorandom number generators and entropy depletion during embedded device boot cycles produce RSA keys that share prime factors with other devices on the internet.

Scaling Batch Greatest Common Divisor (BGCD) Algorithms

David McGrew, Brandon Enright, and Andrew Chi develop high-performance multithreaded tools to run Batch GCD computations across more than 100 million public HTTPS certificates.

Factoring Moduli and Generating Private PEM Keys

Correlating public certificates harvested from active scanning and Certificate Transparency logs identified thousands of vulnerable RSA moduli, immediately computing their private keys.

Auditing and Remediating Weak Public Keys

The authors demonstrate automated certificate auditing pipelines, urging certificate authorities and hardware manufacturers to enforce automated pre-issuance GCD checks.

talks.title: Apple's Predicament: NSPredicate Exploitation on macOS and iOS
talks.teaser: Austin Emmitt demonstrates bypassing Apple's iOS 16 NSPredicate restrictions, achieving 100% reliable PAC bypasses and code execution in SpringBoard.
talks.summary:
The Evolution of NSPredicate Exploitation

Following the infamous FORCEDENTRY zero-click iMessage exploit, Apple introduced strict sandboxing restrictions to prevent NSPredicate from invoking arbitrary Objective-C methods.

Circumventing iOS 16 NSPredicateVisitor Protections

Austin Emmitt discovers syntax manipulation techniques in NSPredicate parsing that completely bypass Apple's AST visitor validations across iOS 16 and macOS.

Reliable Pointer Authentication Code (PAC) Bypasses

Using carefully constructed predicate trees, Emmitt scripts the Objective-C runtime to invoke arbitrary C functions with controlled arguments, achieving a 100% reliable PAC bypass.

Exploiting SpringBoard and System Services

Demonstrating live code injection into core system daemons (including SpringBoard and Preferences) illustrates stealing sensitive notifications, device telemetry, and location data.

talks.title: An Audacious Plan to Halt the Internet's Enshittification (Encore)
talks.teaser: Cory Doctorow delivers an encore analysis on the decay of monopoly web platforms, advocating for aggressive antitrust action and adversarial interoperability.
talks.summary:
Deconstructing Platform Degradation and Lock-In

Cory Doctorow explores the structural causes behind the decline of dominant digital platforms, detailing how monopoly consolidation harms users and business customers alike.

The Threat of Anti-Circumvention Laws

Corporate platforms leverage Section 1201 of the DMCA and Computer Fraud and Abuse Act (CFAA) litigation to criminalize reverse engineering, scrapers, and interoperability tools.

Restoring Digital Sovereignty via Interoperability

Mandating open APIs and legal safe harbors for adversarial interoperability allows third-party developers to build privacy-respecting wrappers around incumbent services.

A Call to Action for Hacker Self-Help

Doctorow calls upon the technical community to develop aggressive self-help tools—including tracker blockers, sideloading tools, and decentralized networks—to reclaim the open web.

talks.title: All Information Looks Like Noise Until You Break the Code
talks.teaser: TSA Administrator David Pekoske, CISA Director Jen Easterly, and CNN's Sean Lyngaas discuss modernizing cybersecurity regulations for US transportation infrastructure.
talks.summary:
Cyber Threats to National Transportation Networks

America's critical pipelines, passenger rail networks, and commercial aviation infrastructure face increasing cyber reconnaissance and ransomware threats from nation-state adversaries.

Shifting from Compliance to Outcome-Based Security

TSA Administrator David Pekoske explains the agency's updated regulatory approach, moving away from rigid checklists toward requiring operators to demonstrate measurable resilience outcomes.

Public-Private Coordination and Threat Sharing

CISA Director Jen Easterly details joint government efforts to provide actionable threat intelligence and vulnerability management support to commercial transport operators.

Engaging the Hacker Community in Critical Infrastructure Defense

The panel invites independent security researchers to collaborate with federal agencies in identifying architectural vulnerabilities and stress-testing industrial transportation systems.

talks.title: Advanced ROP Framework: Pushing ROP to Its Limits
talks.teaser: Dr. Bramwell Brizendine and Davy Kusuma present ROP ROCKET, an automated ROP compiler supporting Heaven's Gate architecture switching and bad-byte gadget synthesis.
talks.summary:
Challenges in Modern Return-Oriented Programming

Constructing reliable ROP chains to bypass Data Execution Prevention (DEP) often fails due to bad character filters in target memory and limited gadget availability.

Introducing the ROP ROCKET Framework

Dr. Bramwell Brizendine and Davy Kusuma unveil ROP ROCKET, an automated ROP chain synthesis framework featuring novel code reuse and gadget transformation primitives.

Heaven's Gate Architecture Switching in ROP

ROCKET invokes specialized ROP Heaven's Gate gadgets to dynamically transition 32-bit processes into 64-bit execution mode at runtime, dramatically expanding available gadget space.

Automated Syscall Invocations and Bad-Byte Gadget Obfuscation

Using direct Windows syscalls rather than Win32 APIs enables automatic DEP bypasses, while algebraic gadget synthesis allows utilizing gadgets whose addresses contain forbidden bytes.

talks.title: Abusing CAN Bus Spec for DoS in Embedded Systems
talks.teaser: Martin Petran explores exploiting edge cases in the CAN bus protocol specification and message metadata fields to induce denial-of-service across embedded ECUs.
talks.summary:
The Absolute Truth of Protocol Specifications

Controller Area Network (CAN) bus implementations strictly adhere to formal ISO standards, leading embedded firmware developers to make dangerous assumptions about message formats.

Violating Specification Assumptions in CAN Frames

Martin Petran evaluates what occurs when an adversary crafts non-compliant CAN messages, manipulating reserved metadata bits and unexpected payload lengths.

Triggering Denial-of-Service in Commercial Driver Stacks

Auditing proprietary and open-source CAN transceivers and microcontroller driver libraries revealed unhandled exceptions and buffer state desynchronizations that freeze embedded controllers.

Defensive Verification for Automotive Software

The author provides test suites and defensive software patterns for embedded developers to validate raw CAN frames safely without relying on hardware-level assumptions.

talks.title: A SSLippery Slope: Unraveling Hidden Dangers of Certificate Misuse
talks.teaser: Bill Demirkapi uncovers systemic validation flaws in digital signature implementations, allowing attackers to repurpose incompatible certificates to sign untrusted code.
talks.summary:
The Critical Role of Code Signing Certificates

Digital code signing certificates undergo rigorous identity vetting to establish publisher trust, ensuring operating systems only execute authenticated binaries and firmware updates.

Discovering Systemic Signature Validation Flaws

Bill Demirkapi investigates parsing logic across major operating system loaders and signature verification APIs, discovering critical oversights in Enhanced Key Usage (EKU) checks.

Bypassing Trust Boundaries with Incompatible Certificates

Vulnerable verifiers mistakenly accept signatures generated by cheap or unrelated TLS/S-MIME certificates as valid code signing credentials, allowing adversaries to sign malicious payloads.

Hardening Cryptographic Verification Pipelines

The author outlines comprehensive remediation steps for operating system developers and software vendors to strictly enforce certificate purpose constraints and signature chain validation.

talks.title: A Series of Unfortunate Events: War Stories in Bug Hunting
talks.teaser: Ben Sadeghipour (NahamSec) and Corben Leo share war stories from high-impact bug bounty engagements across prisons, major tech firms, and online casinos.
talks.summary:
High-Stakes Vulnerability Hunting in the Wild

Top bug bounty hunters encounter complex architectures spanning diverse industries, uncovering unexpected vulnerabilities with massive real-world impact.

Breaching Enterprise Prison Management Systems

Ben Sadeghipour and Corben Leo detail discovering critical authentication bypasses in correctional facility management software, granting full administrative access to sensitive inmate records.

Publishing Spoofed News on Major Tech Portals

The authors recount discovering CMS logic flaws that allowed unauthorized content publication directly onto the front pages of major global technology corporations.

Escalating Privilege in Online Gaming and Casinos

Dissecting logic vulnerabilities and API authorization oversights in leading online gaming platforms illustrates the severe financial and operational impact of chainable bugs.

talks.title: A Pain in the NAS: Exploiting Cloud Connectivity to Pwn Your NAS
talks.teaser: Claroty Team82 reveals how cloud connectivity features in Western Digital and Synology NAS devices allow remote compromise and full RCE across millions of devices.
talks.summary:
The Architecture of Cloud-Connected Storage Appliances

Modern Network-Attached Storage (NAS) appliances feature cloud relay services that allow consumers to remotely access local files from mobile apps without configuring router port forwarding.

Reverse Engineering Device Cloud Pairing Protocols

Noam Moshe and Sharon Brizinov analyze the mutual authentication protocols used by Western Digital and Synology cloud platforms, discovering flawed device identifier validation.

Device Impersonation and Token Theft via Certificate Transparency

Harvesting device metadata from Certificate Transparency logs allowed the researchers to spoof NAS identities, conduct targeted phishing, and steal cloud proxy authorization tokens.

Full Remote Code Execution at Pwn2Own Toronto

Chaining device authentication flaws with local API memory corruption enabled bypassing firewalls to achieve full remote code execution across cloud-connected NAS devices.

talks.title: A Different Uber Post-Mortem
talks.teaser: Former Uber CSO Joe Sullivan provides an inside retrospective on the 2016 Uber data breach, executive liability, and the criminalization of incident response.
talks.summary:
The Historic Prosecution of a Chief Security Officer

The federal criminal prosecution of former Uber Chief Security Officer Joe Sullivan (United States v. Sullivan) marked a watershed moment for executive liability in corporate incident response.

Inside the 2016 AWS Credential Intrusion

Joe Sullivan recounts the technical reality of the 2016 incident, where external researchers accessed Uber AWS infrastructure via exposed GitHub credentials and demanded payment.

Distinguishing Security Researchers from Criminal Extortionists

Sullivan details his team’s investigation and interactions with the young hackers, exploring the ambiguous legal boundary between aggressive bug bounty submissions and extortion.

Lessons for Corporate Governance and Legal Transparency

The talk examines critical lessons regarding executive accountability, transparent disclosure to regulatory bodies, and the unintended consequences of criminalizing CISO decision-making.

talks.title: Review on the Less Traveled Road: 9 Years of Overlooked MikroTik Pre-Auth RCE
talks.teaser: DEVCORE researcher NiNi Chen discloses a 9-year-old pre-authentication remote code execution zero-day in MikroTik RouterOS affecting over 3 million devices.
talks.summary:
The Attack Surface of MikroTik RouterOS

MikroTik RouterOS powers over three million enterprise and ISP networking devices globally, making it a high-priority target for state-sponsored threat actors.

Analyzing IPC Mechanisms and the Nova Message Architecture

Ting-Yu Chen (NiNi) investigates the undocumented internal architecture of RouterOS, moving beyond standard Nova Message research into low-level socket callbacks and remote objects.

Discovering a 9-Year-Old Pre-Auth RCE Zero-Day

Uncovering an architectural race condition in lower-layer remote object management revealed a pre-authentication remote code execution flaw present in all active RouterOS releases since 2014.

Winning Master of Pwn and Tool Release

Chen reviews the Pwn2Own Toronto exploit implementation, releasing open-source reverse-engineering tooling to help the research community audit RouterOS systems.

talks.title: A Broken Marriage: Abusing Mixed Vendor Kerberos Stacks
talks.teaser: Ceri Coburn demonstrates privilege escalation across mixed-vendor environments where Linux/Unix MIT and Heimdal Kerberos stacks integrate with Windows Active Directory.
talks.summary:
Interoperability in Mixed-Vendor Kerberos Realms

Enterprise environments frequently integrate Linux, macOS, and Unix hosts running open-source MIT or Heimdal Kerberos stacks into Windows Active Directory domains.

Proprietary Extensions vs. Open Protocol Standards

Ceri Coburn highlights fundamental architectural incompatibilities between Microsoft's proprietary Kerberos PAC extensions and standard POSIX identity mapping in open-source Kerberos stacks.

Exploiting Identity Discrepancies for Cross-Platform Elevation

Exploiting configuration weaknesses in domain-joined Linux systems allows attackers to forge authorization attributes, escalating privileges across Unix endpoints joined to Active Directory.

Enhancing Rubeus for Mixed-Vendor Exploitation

Coburn demonstrates an updated release of the Rubeus toolkit, equipping red-team operators with automated capabilities to exploit cross-realm Kerberos delegation flaws.

talks.title: #NoFilter: Abusing Windows Filtering Platform for Privilege Escalation
talks.teaser: Ron Ben Yizhak introduces #NoFilter, a novel privilege escalation technique abusing the Windows Filtering Platform to achieve SYSTEM execution without token manipulation.
talks.summary:
The Limitations of Classic Windows Privilege Escalation

Traditional tools that escalate to NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM (such as Potato exploits and token stealers) manipulate access tokens and service handles, making them heavily monitored by EDR rules.

Reverse Engineering the Windows Filtering Platform (WFP)

Ron Ben Yizhak explores the built-in Windows Filtering Platform kernel subsystem, examining the Base Filtering Engine (BFE), TCPIP driver interfaces, and IPSec configuration.

Abusing RPC Methods for Undetected Execution

By manipulating undocumented RPC methods exposed by WFP system services, an unprivileged user can coerce kernel components to execute arbitrary processes as SYSTEM.

Evading Modern EDR Detections with #NoFilter

Demonstrating the open-source #NoFilter tool shows how abusing native network filtering components achieves full local privilege escalation while remaining completely invisible to behavioral sensors.

talks.title: Welcome to DEF CON 31
talks.teaser: DEF CON Founder Jeff Moss (The Dark Tangent) officially kicks off DEF CON 31, welcoming hackers from around the globe to Las Vegas.

talks.title: Tracking the World's Dumbest Cyber Mercenaries
talks.teaser: EFF researcher Cooper Quintin recounts tracking Dark Caracal, a Lebanese state-backed cyber-mercenary group whose comical operational security blunders exposed their operations.
talks.summary:
Tracking the Dark Caracal Mercenary Group

For over six years, Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF) researchers monitored Dark Caracal, a state-aligned cyber-mercenary group operating out of Lebanon targeting journalists and dissidents.

Hilarious Operational Security Failures

Cooper Quintin highlights unbelievable OPSEC mistakes committed by the group—including leaving C2 control panels unauthenticated, running surveillance apps from personal test devices, and exposing target databases.

The Surprising Efficacy of Low-Skill Threat Actors

Despite rudimentary tradecraft, Dark Caracal successfully compromised thousands of victims worldwide by deploying off-the-shelf mobile malware via phishing.

Insights into the Commercial Surveillance Industry

Quintin analyzes the growing market for budget cyber mercenaries, emphasizing that even unsophisticated actors pose serious threats to vulnerable human rights defenders.

talks.title: Making the DEF CON 31 Badge
talks.teaser: Badge designer Mar Williams explains the creative inspiration, embedded engineering, and production challenges behind the official DEF CON 31 electronic badge.

talks.title: Secretary of the Department of Homeland Security at DEF CON 31
talks.teaser: US Secretary of Homeland Security Alejandro Mayorkas joins Jeff Moss for a fireside chat on federal cybersecurity priorities, critical infrastructure, and hacker engagement.
